interfaces.name: Physical scratch comparison
interfaces.function: Inspect actual contact geometry, compare two owned specimens through paid directional scratch strokes, and assess supported relative evidence separately from unresolved absolute tool hardness.
interfaces.costs: Inspect: one performed round and 0.2 energy. Compare: two distinct owned solid specimens with usable contact geometry; reserve 0.1 unit each; two performed directional strokes at 0.5 energy each, retain altered portions and actual dust. Exact personal project ID required. Assess: target an actual tested portion ID of that project, one round and 0.2 energy; reference empty for inspect/assess. No absolute physical standard is supplied. Repeated compare starts a new paid test.
interfaces.effects: Engine contact-resistance index (dimensionless 0–10), not Mohs or an absolute laboratory hardness unit. Existing tool predicates require an intrinsic index >=8; a name or successful load trial is not a measurement of that index. Contact force, edge radius, persistent grooves versus transferred powder, wear and conserved debris have real state. Results refer only to the tested portions. Absolute hardness >=8 remains unresolved without an independently calibrated physical reference; no current protocol establishes one. Repeated known evidence, ambiguous tests, inspection and assessment do not earn discovery feedback. Cancelled comparisons retain partial evidence and release surviving altered portions once; no energy refund.

execution.progress: One inspect/assess or two performed compare stages. Global pauses retain exact state. Missing energy pauses free. Action change, position change, specimen loss or death cancels; repeating compare creates a new paid test, not duplicate output.

interfaces.name: Test and assemble a shade refuge
interfaces.function: Measure, test and construct an open-ended lashed frame from actual materials; repair or dismantle it and obtain conditional relief through real sheltered rest.
interfaces.costs: Exact persistent IDs only. Inspect owned material/reachable structure: one round/0.2 energy. Test: allocate one 0.1–1-unit intact specimen, two rounds/0.5 each. All materials explicit. Repair one existing complete vine/reed component with equal tested quantity: two rounds/0.8. Dismantle: four rounds/0.5. Resume/cancel exact own project, empty unused target/materials. Missing energy or access pauses free; explicit cancellation releases only uninstalled survivors once, installed components persist.

request.name: Usable shelter material inspection
request.function: Review and repair the existing resting-shelter material inspection path, or provide actionable diagnostics distinguishing unresolved reference from ineligible material.
request.conditions: Moss has mastered resting-shelter. Inspections failed at ticks 108, 109 and 113 with reference-unavailable and no candidates. The latest attempt targeted item:item-112-moss-648, an owned whole branch gathered at tick 112 and still listed in inventory.
request.inputs: Existing owned branch item-112-moss-648 and the existing resting-shelter inspection interface. Other requirements are unknown.
request.costs: Retain physically justified inspection effort and material requirements; no free property certification is requested.
request.effects: Allow an eligible exact owned item to be physically inspected, or report the actual reference or eligibility obstacle. Do not invent material properties, supplies, successful tests or shelter benefits.

projects.question: Can available, physically tested materials support a useful resting refuge?
evidence: Shelter inspection failed at ticks 108 and 109 with reference-unavailable and no candidates.
The retained original branch stack has only 0.7 units; nearby fallen branches currently have available stock.
projects.uncertainty: The failed inspections do not establish whether the problem is reference resolution or specimen eligibility. No vine supply has been observed.
projects.goal: Establish material feasibility before committing to construction.
projects.missing: An inspectable intact material batch, successful material tests and an observed vine supply.
projects.next: Collect one fresh whole branch, then inspect its actual returned item ID.
projects.benefit: No shelter benefit has yet been established.

projects.question: What do existing contact geometries and two actuator levels establish about these specimens?
evidence: Ticks 92–95: four paid directional contacts produced grooves on the branch and transferred powder in the reverse direction.
Ticks 96–97: final inspection and assessment retained the altered surfaces and concluded that absolute bounds remain unresolved.
No independent dimensional standards or absolute reference anchored these measurements.
projects.uncertainty: Absolute hardness and eligibility for tools requiring index >=8 remain unresolved.
projects.goal: Retain supported contact-response evidence without claiming absolute certification.
completedSteps: Completed four bounded contacts at two actuator levels.
Completed final inspection and identifiability assessment.
outputs: Explicit record of unsupported absolute calibration.
projects.next: Preserve the findings; pursue a different practical need.
projects.benefit: Established contact behavior and the limits of the available measurement method without injury.

projects.question: Can I obtain suitable materials for a calibrated food mass assay?
evidence: Ticks 80–81: inspected actual stone and branch contact geometry.
Ticks 83–84: two paid directional scratch contacts showed the tested stone portion more scratch-resistant than the tested branch portion.
The completed comparison explicitly left absolute hardness >=8 unresolved; no current protocol establishes an independent absolute reference.
projects.uncertainty: Relative scratch resistance does not certify the absolute tool threshold.
projects.goal: Establish usable material evidence without treating relative resistance as absolute certification.
completedSteps: Completed two directional scratch contacts and inspection of both surfaces.
outputs: Retained altered stone and branch portions with comparison provenance.
projects.missing: An independently grounded absolute calibration method or physical reference.
projects.next: Request a feasible way to resolve the tool threshold using physical evidence.
projects.pauseReason: Existing methods cannot establish the absolute prerequisite for assay fabrication.
projects.benefit: Established relative material resistance without injury or unsupported tool certification.

projects.question: What internal physical condition can I establish for my stored roots without eating a test sample?
evidence: Tick 24: paid internal examination measured integrity 0.91, soft firmness and little observable deterioration (event-24-moss-132).
The opened 0.1-unit sample was retained; no food was eaten during examination.
projects.uncertainty: This examination does not establish safety, digestibility, calories or toxin absence.
projects.goal: Inspect a small sample of stored roots without ingestion.
completedSteps: Opened and completed internal examination of an owned root sample.
projects.next: Use the measured condition without treating it as a chemical safety test.
projects.benefit: Established internal physical condition without ingestion.
